content.title: Conceptual Design of a 5 MV High-Voltage System for a Compact Orbitron Fusion Device
content.abstract: The high-voltage system is a key part of the puzzle toward achieving net-positive fusion power in a compact Orbitron device. This paper presents a conceptual engineering design for a 5 MV, 20 mA, 100 kW HV system for a next-generation Orbitron, serving as an upper-bound design point for the HV system. The MC-TRANS++ 0-D code is used to set the load requirements: a 1 m long, 0.45 m first-wall-radius central cell, 2.5 T on-axis and 10 T mirror-throat fields, and a 5 MV radial potential drop sustaining supersonic rotation ($M = 4.8$). This delivers a triple product of $5.8 \times 10^{21}$ keV s /
